text_blocks.snippet: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) causes high blood pressure in the arteries of your lungs, leading to symptoms like shortness of breath and extreme tiredness as the right side of the heart works harder.
snippet_highlighted_words: shortness of breath and extreme tiredness

text_blocks.snippet: In the early stages, you might not notice any signs. As the condition progresses, common symptoms include:

list.snippet: Shortness of breath (dyspnea) during daily activities like climbing stairs or exercising
Dizziness or lightheadedness, which can lead to fainting
Swelling (edema) in the ankles, feet, legs, or abdomen due to fluid buildup
Heart palpitations or a racing, pounding heartbeat
Bluish lips or fingers (cyanosis) caused by low oxygen levels

text_blocks.snippet: Learn more about managing these signs through the American Lung Association or consult the Mayo Clinic for comprehensive medical details.
If you or someone you know is experiencing these signs, tell me:

list.snippet: Are you experiencing symptoms at rest or only during activity?
